span: We utilized data across three cohorts/biobanks, focusing on three types of multi-omics data known for wide-spread missing values (methylation, proteomics, and metabolomics).

assumptions: multiple modalities available for the same individuals
conclusion: The methods and benchmarks do not exploit information across different multi-omics modalities.
scope: Applies to the evaluated methods including the FLASH extension.
span: Firstly, none of the methods or benchmarks we used take advantage of information across different multi-omics modalities, especially when data for the same set of individuals is available, as in the case of the ROSMAP and MSBB datasets in our study with RNA-seq, methylation and proteomics features measured.

conclusion: The analysis is limited to proteomics, metabolomics and methylation and does not assess other xQTL data types such as single-cell or single-nucleotide RNA-seq.
scope: Limitation of evaluation scope, not proof that the method cannot handle those data.
span: Secondly, our analysis was confined to proteomics, metabolomics, and methylation data. We did not assess the impact of missing data and imputation methods on other xQTL data types, particularly single cell or single nucleotide RNA-seq, though there are existing benchmarks and recommendations for these data types[28].

objects: generic imputation; functional data; methylation; penalized functional regression
conclusion: The authors did not explore domain-specific functional approaches and identify functional-data extensions of FLASH as future work.
scope: Untested potential for methylation imputation; no comparative guarantee is supplied.
span: Thirdly, the imputation methods we employed are generic. There is potential for future development of methods tailored to specific data types, for example matrix factorization methods — possibly by extending FLASH — for functional data such as methylation. We did not explore domain-specific approaches, such as penalized functional regression, which might offer better results for methylation imputation[29].

objects: D: n by p data matrix; variable Dj; Yobs; Ymiss; Xobs; Xmiss
assumptions: imputation of variable j using the other variables
conclusion: MissXGB partitions each target variable into observed and missing responses and partitions other variables into corresponding predictor subsets.
span: Specifically, a data matrix Dn×p can be divided into four parts based on any given j-th variable Dj (a length-n vector): Yobs, Ymiss, Xobs, and Xmiss. Here, Yobs represents the observed values of Dj, while Ymiss denotes its unobserved values. Variables other than j in the dataset are partitioned into Xobs amd Xmiss for observed and missing values respectively.

scope: Named-method relation stated in the overview.

objects: observed responses and predictors; predicted missing responses; iterated imputed matrix
conclusion: MissXGB trains XGBoost on observed responses and predictors, predicts missing responses, and stops when the difference between successive imputed matrices first increases.
scope: Operational stopping rule; neither convergence nor accuracy is guaranteed by this statement.
span: Overall, for each column Xmiss, a XGBoost model is trained with response Yobs and predictors Xobs. The trained model is then applied to predict Ymiss with Xmiss. The iteration will stop as soon as the difference between the newly imputed data matrix and the previous one increases for the first time.
